content.text:
No, not all of them. Of the 26 upstream lines, two hooks have no fork-side alternative for their goal. The printer-agent override is not needed to connect a printer; it only serves an extra requirement. Part of the gizmo change is dead code.

| Change | Needed? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Wizard flag (`GUI_App`, 4 lines) | **Yes** | Orca opens the wizard when the config file didn't exist at startup (`m_app_conf_exists`, a private field) or when only default printers are installed. Neither can be changed from outside Orca's code without a hack, such as writing a config file early. |
| Printer-agent override (`GUI_App`, 10 lines) | **No, not for connecting** | See below. |
| Canvas overlay callback (`GLCanvas3D`, 6 lines) | **Yes, given the design** | `GLCanvas3D::render()` has no hook for drawing inside its ImGui frame (ImGui is the canvas's own UI layer). The alternative is native wx controls on top of the OpenGL canvas. I didn't test that, but I'd expect it to be unreliable across platforms. |
| `reset_rotation()` wrapper | **Yes** | It depends on `m_init_rotation_scale_tran`, which is private. The fork can't reproduce it. |
| `reset_scale()` wrapper | **Not strictly** | The fork could get the same result through public calls: `Plater::TakeSnapshot` plus `on_change("scale", axis, 100)` for each axis. That means copying 3 lines instead of adding 1 line upstream. Reasonable either way. |
| `reset_position()` wrapper | **No, it's unused** | Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` or `tests/` calls it. This line can be removed. |

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

I made both changes in a new worktree. The fork now adds 15 lines to upstream OrcaSlicer files instead of 26, and all three shell harness modes I ran pass. Nothing is committed yet; the worktree is at `.claude/worktrees/drop-upstream-extras` on branch `claude/drop-upstream-extras`, cut from 886098514b.

**Upstream changes removed (11 lines):**
- **Unused gizmo wrapper:** deleted the `reset_position()` line from `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp`.
- **Printer-agent override:** deleted from `GUI_App.hpp` (the field, its comment and `#include <utility>`) and from `switch_printer_agent()` in `GUI_App.cpp`.

What's left upstream: the 4-line wizard flag, the 6-line canvas overlay callback, and the `reset_rotation()` and `reset_scale()` wrappers.

**Fork-side replacements:**
- **Connecting a Bambu printer:** `OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection` again creates the Bambu agent and installs it directly, using public calls, as 67577ad993 did. I added one line that commit didn't have: it refreshes the sidebar's printer dropdowns, which Orca's own agent switch also does.
- **Shell teardown:** `ShellController::uninstall()` now always calls `switch_printer_agent()`, so the printer profile chooses the agent again. It does nothing when the agent already matches the profile.
- **Harness:** the check "explicit provider survives profile re-evaluation" became "profile re-evaluation replaces the connection provider" plus "connecting again reinstalls it". I also removed a stock-mode check that only tested the deleted field.

**Test results** (a fresh RelWithDebInfo build, with the web pages built):

| Harness mode | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `--printer-setup` (runs the fake-Bambu connection flow and the new checks) | 124 | all pass |
| default (includes the shell uninstall checks) | 412 | all pass |
| `--stock` | 24 | all pass (25 before, minus the removed check) |

**Behavior change to accept or reject:** you now lose a Bambu printer's connection when you select a non-Bambu printer profile. Before this change, the connection survived that switch. Home will show the printer's status as unknown until you reconnect, and reconnecting works; the harness checks that. This matches stock Orca. If you'd rather keep the connection, drop this branch and keep the override.

git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Connect Bambu printers without patching Orca's agent switch

The fork added lines to two OrcaSlicer files that it does not need:

- GUI_App gained a printer_agent_override field, applied inside
  switch_printer_agent(), so that a Bambu connection made from Home would
  survive a change to a non-Bambu printer profile. Connecting itself never
  needed it: the Bambu agent can be created with the public
  NetworkAgentFactory and installed with NetworkAgent::set_printer_agent,
  which is what OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection does again now.
- GizmoObjectManipulation gained a reset_position() wrapper that nothing calls.

Removing both leaves 15 fork lines in upstream files instead of 26. All
removals are of fork-added lines; no upstream line is deleted or moved.
GUI_App.hpp is byte-identical to its state before 9f739dccf2.

Behavior change: selecting a non-Bambu printer profile now hands the
agent back to Orca's profile-driven choice, as stock Orca does, so a
Bambu printer's live status on Home goes stale until it is connected
again. Connecting again reinstalls the Bambu agent. Shell teardown now
always calls switch_printer_agent() so the profile picks the agent again;
the call does nothing when the agent already matches.

prepare_connection also refreshes the sidebar's preset dropdowns after
installing the agent, as switch_printer_agent() does, since the sync-AMS
button depends on the agent.

Tests: the shell harness now checks that profile re-evaluation replaces
the connection agent, that connecting again reinstalls it, and that the
reconnected printer delivers fresh data. The stock-mode check that only
guarded the removed field is gone. On a fresh macOS RelWithDebInfo build
with web pages built: --printer-setup 124/124, default 412/412,
--stock 24/24 checks pass.

Rebase check: git merge-tree against upstream/main 7ca2b9ad9c (merge base
3ffb9585d2). Before this commit GUI_App.hpp, GUI_App.cpp and GLCanvas3D.cpp
conflict; after it, GUI_App.hpp no longer conflicts. GUI_App.cpp conflicts
as a single whole-file block both before and after, so this change does not
alter it.
EOF
